best_for: People who already use Viber on their phone and want to read, type and take calls on a computer keyboard and screen.

points.title: Your phone comes first
points.text: Viber for Desktop syncs with your mobile account, so you need Viber installed and active on a phone before the desktop app will activate. It does not work as a standalone account.

points.title: Free calls, paid calls out
points.text: Messages and Viber-to-Viber calls are free between people who both have the app.

points.title: Windows 10 or later for the main build
points.text: The current Windows build is 64-bit for Windows 10, Windows 11 and Windows 11 on ARM. Viber's site has a separate 32-bit installer for 32-bit Windows and Windows 8 or lower.

points.title: Mac and Linux options
points.text: Viber's download page lists macOS 10.15 and up, with a separate build for 10.11 to 10.14. On Linux it offers .deb, .rpm and AppImage; the Flatpak listed here is verified by Flathub as published by Viber Media, x64 only.

points.title: Closed source
points.text: The app is proprietary and free to download. Flathub marks its license as proprietary under Viber's terms of use.

points.title: Version history is on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 66 versions as a machine-wide 64-bit installer. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
